title: Open Hours
briefing: Runner, over here. The gate is open, but Nella cannot feed the families coming through it: the concession has locked her water. First, take Oru’s welcome record so we can do both jobs on one trip. Then read the shutoff notice at the Commons exchange. I will stay on your channel until the kitchen is running.
completion: There. Water in the pot, opening hours on the channel. The first family is through the gate. You made a promise we can keep for tonight. Take your welcome record back to Oru, then find Nella west of the exchange. She knows why this bill keeps coming back.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Both records ready? Good. Go to the Commons exchange, at the center of the plaza. Press E to read the shutoff notice. I am on your channel.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: The notice calls this an unpaid account. Nella calls it supper. Follow the marker to the water meter; restore both controls, clear the enforcement machines, then hold the meter’s ring.

steps.text: Post the opening hours after the kitchen feed is restored. Press E, then return to Iri.
steps.voice: I can hear the pump. Good work. Go to the Relay terminal and press E to post the opening hours. Then come back to me; I owe you a proper welcome.

story.speaker: iri
story.invitation: New signal? Iri Vale, by the Commons gate. Six families need a meal, and Nella’s kitchen has lost its water. Come here. I will walk you through it.

title: Receipts for Air
briefing: Stallholders are paying freight charges on goods they carry in themselves. Pull the billing record from the Commons exchange for Iri.
completion: The bill names a lift demolished nineteen years ago. Iri circles the contract number and asks for the receipts.

title: The Unpaid Minute
briefing: The crossing waits a full minute for a toll payment it can no longer accept. Reset the Relay terminal to a timed pedestrian crossing.
completion: The lights change. A carrier gets her cart across before the next freight convoy.

title: A Courier Stands Still
briefing: Two audit drones keep tagging a resting courier as abandoned cargo. Disable them before they drag him back to the depot.
completion: The courier sits down again. His lunch is still warm.

title: The Missing Footpath
briefing: Check the water carriers' path at the Fen drawdown gauge, east of Vesper. Iri needs room for relief carts; Mara wants the drilling rigs kept off the reed bank.
completion: The carts will fit without cutting the bank. Iri marks the route, then adds a barrier the concession's rigs cannot clear.

title: Names below the Arrows
briefing: The route node sends visitors straight past Copper Walk. Its homes are missing from the register. Add the residents' directions at the Relay terminal.
completion: Copper Walk appears on the display. Someone has already submitted a correction for the kitchen entrance.

title: Deadweight Fee
briefing: Wirejacks are hauling public handcarts into a salvage depot. Disable the collectors so the carriers can take their carts back.
completion: The carts come back with bent handles and most of their wheels. Iri opens the repair rack.

title: Hold the Middle Landing
briefing: Lift stewards cannot open a service panel without audit drones reporting a fare violation. Clear the drones while they reconnect the middle landing's call button.
completion: The button lights up. A child presses it three times before the steward asks him to stop.

title: A Map with Room
briefing: Fetch the original access survey from the Public memory archive. The current map routes wheelchairs into stairs and treats reed banks as spare road space.
completion: Iri restores the turning spaces and removes a freight lane to make room. Its operators arrive at the desk with a bill.

title: The Right to Arrive Late
briefing: The delivery contract fines families when their courier stops to help someone. Post the replacement terms at the Commons exchange: report delays, waive the penalties.
completion: A late parcel arrives with a note explaining the detour. The recipient signs for it and asks whether the other patient is all right.

title: The Road through Roots
briefing: Survey the old service path at Cinderwood's Canopy refuge. It may carry relief carts without cutting through the last living trees.
completion: The detour works, but it takes longer. Carriers raise their prices; Iri revises the food budget.

title: Two Ends of a Promise
briefing: A route has been marked open without testing the lift at the far end. Run a return check at the Relay terminal before anyone follows it.
completion: The cabin is stuck two floors short. Iri cancels the opening and calls the lift crew.

title: The Toll Collector Sleeps
briefing: A debt warden is enforcing permits from the vanished council. Shut it down so the crossing stewards can remove the old toll schedule.
completion: The barrier is open. The stewards post their maintenance rota on its empty control box.

title: Routes without Witnesses
briefing: The traffic archive stores names beside every journey. At the Memory vault, strip personal routes from the public congestion report.
completion: The traffic totals remain. Iri checks that a search for her own journeys returns nothing.

title: The Copper Walk Compact
briefing: The lower-deck stewards will maintain the network if they can control closures and repairs in their districts. Register their compact at the Commons exchange.
completion: Iri hands over the exclusive access key. Copper Walk files its first repair request without going through her.

title: The Gate Faces Outward
briefing: Survey the road beyond the South floodgate. Mark the water stops, shade, and last safe turnback before the pavement gives way to salt.
completion: The route is mapped. A trader at the first water stop has already changed his prices.

title: A Light under Salt
briefing: The Last salt beacon still broadcasts harbor directions. Update it for the dry basin and add a painted route marker for power failures.
completion: The transmitter cuts out halfway through the test. The painted arrow still points home.

title: No Empty Country
briefing: Visit the Glassroot soil core north of Vesper. Mark the homes and the well's catchment before the next route survey calls the steppe vacant.
completion: Iri includes the settlement and roots in the map. She refuses a mineral broker's request for the underlying survey.

title: A Machine at Every Horizon
briefing: Audit drones have followed the beacon signal to the roadside shelters. Disable the trackers before they register the shelters as unpaid toll stations.
completion: The shelter beacons stay on. Iri removes the collectors' tracking addresses from the relay list.

title: The Direction of Welcome
briefing: The Last salt beacon only gives directions back to Vesper. Add the outward routes and their current supply limits.
completion: Both directions are listed. The board also says which water stop has run dry.

title: Water Is Not Freight
briefing: Wirejacks are stripping cooling fins from public water carriers. Clear the collection route before the next shelter delivery.
completion: The carriers leave on time. The recovered fins go into the roadside repair stock.

title: The Long Return
briefing: The short water route cuts through the bank protecting the fen's remaining well. Check the longer path at the drawdown gauge and report its carrying time.
completion: The detour protects the bank but cuts daily deliveries. Iri posts the reduced ration beside the new route.

title: The Price of a Signal
briefing: The Relay terminal rejects basin messages unless the sender owns the surrounding land. Replace the deed check with a local maintenance signature.
completion: The roadside crews connect using their own station records. The first message requests replacement batteries.

title: Sunset Inspection
briefing: Wardens are challenging the roadside crews' maintenance signatures. Disable their relays while the stewards copy the records to independent ledgers.
completion: The copies are safe. A burned relay identifies the next collector in the outer toll chain.

title: The Last Proprietary Mile
briefing: Retrieve the outer toll chain's founding clause from the Public memory archive. Iri thinks its emergency authority expired with the harbor evacuation.
completion: The toll order expired years ago. The water concessions did not. Iri separates the two stacks of contracts.

title: A Closure with a Date
briefing: Install an expiry clock at the South floodgate. Every closure must name a steward, give a reason, and set a review date.
completion: The current closure now ends on Friday unless a named steward renews it. The appeal address fits on the same screen.

title: Static on the Salt
briefing: Fee-notice drones are flooding the basin frequency ahead of a dust front. Shut down the repeaters so distress calls can reach the beacons.
completion: A repair crew's stranded-vehicle call comes through. Iri sends their coordinates before the dust reaches the road.

title: Four Hands on the Key
briefing: Divide the Relay terminal's master access between district, roadside, accessibility, and maintenance delegates. The charter must also bar loans secured against the fen or steppe.
completion: Iri keeps a mechanic's key. The rejected collateral deal leaves three bridges without repair funding; she posts their names.

title: The Toll Chain Breaks
briefing: The outer toll wardens are still executing their final order. Disable them while the stewards broadcast the expiry record.
completion: The last barrier drops. A route crew checks the surface before letting the waiting carts through.

title: An Arrow for the Lost
briefing: Reserve the Last salt beacon's batteries for distress calls and publish the fen's reduced water schedule. Scheduled carriers will have to wait for new cells.
completion: A stranded traveler's call gets through. Three carriers miss their slots. Iri logs the rescue and the delays together.

title: Low Water
briefing: Walk the reopened route to the Fen drawdown gauge. Iri needs a fresh reading before the stewards set next month's crossings and water deliveries.
completion: The gauge is lower. Iri posts rationed crossings and turns down an offer to buy priority access. The repair fund has enough for another month.

title: A Place for Your Name
briefing: Before we file your arrival, look at the kitchen queue. Those people donated water. The concession has charged them for it again and locked the feed. Speak to Oru first; their welcome record belongs in this case. Then read the notice at the Commons exchange. We will preserve what happened, and get the kitchen open.
completion: The feed is running, and the original notice is safe in the vault. A record cannot feed anyone. Today we managed both. Finish your introduction with Oru, then ask Nella about the names missing from her kitchen tally.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Start with the original. The Commons exchange is in the center of the plaza. Press E to read the shutoff notice; keep the record intact.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: Keep the notice intact. It is evidence. Follow the marker to the two water controls. Clear the enforcement machines and remain in the meter’s ring until the feed is steady.

steps.text: Register the witnesses who kept the kitchen open. Press E, then return to Sera.
steps.voice: The water has returned. Now bring the notice to the Memory vault and press E to preserve it. Return to me afterward; no one gets to rewrite what you saw.

story.speaker: sera
story.invitation: I am Sera Quill, beside the Commons. The kitchen has been charged for water its neighbors already donated. Come speak with me. We need a witness, and a working feed.

title: The Borrowed Lullaby
briefing: A commercial catalog is using a resident's lullaby recording without permission. Check the release at the Memory vault. The melody can stay public; the singer's voice cannot.
completion: The recording is withdrawn. The neighborhood keeps the tune and credits its singer.

title: A Signature Can Expire
briefing: A diary's permission seal expired after one winter. Retrieve the dated instruction from the Public memory archive and close the open copy.
completion: The diary returns to its intended readers. Its expiry date is visible on the access panel.

title: Collectors of Echoes
briefing: Audit drones are taking voiceprints from the memory clinic queue. Disable their recorders before another patient is scanned.
completion: Sera seals the damaged recorders for evidence. She does not play them back.

title: An Empty Shelf
briefing: The vault sells a recording of birds returning to Mourning Fen. Compare the field record at the drawdown gauge with its source file.
completion: The calls came from a sales library. Sera marks the species absent and files the unedited survey beside the advertisement.

title: The Witness and the Owner
briefing: A stallholder's lift-accident testimony includes a private family argument. Post the safety account at the Commons exchange with that section removed.
completion: The lift inspection is ordered. The witness checks the public version and asks Sera to keep the original sealed.

title: The Index Disagrees
briefing: Salvage machines are restoring files whose owners requested deletion. Disable the recovery units before they make more copies.
completion: The recovery queue stops. Sera takes the machine log for the deletion hearing.

title: Glass with a Handle
briefing: The Memory vault hides withdrawal controls three menus deep. Fit a panel showing who has access, for what purpose, and for how long.
completion: A visitor changes her permissions without calling Sera over. She leaves the panel open for the next person.

title: A Date Is Not a Person
briefing: Two residents share a birth date and a former address. The Public memory archive has merged their records. Split them and keep a correction trail.
completion: Their appointments separate. So do their debts; one resident immediately asks for a second correction.

title: The Room without Playback
briefing: A witness to Cinderwood's false restoration accounts will meet only at the Canopy refuge. Check the approach for company recorders.
completion: The approach is clear. The witness signs a limited release, then asks what happens to the pension fund holding those certificates.

title: The Shape of a Refusal
briefing: The Memory vault turns unanswered requests into permission after a timeout. Change the default so a record stays closed until its owner answers.
completion: Sera leaves the test request unanswered. The seal stays shut.

title: Public Truth, Private Wounds
briefing: Prepare the lift-failure inquiry at the Public memory archive using machine logs and testimony witnesses have released. Keep disputed points marked.
completion: The evidence is enough to order repairs. The report lists the questions the inquiry still cannot answer.

title: The Keeper at the Lock
briefing: An archive warden is blocking valid withdrawals under the old access rules. Disable its lock controls so the clinic can honor them.
completion: The owners regain access to their records. Sera adds the warden's order to the policy appeal.

title: Sera’s Missing Week
briefing: The Memory vault claims to hold Sera's missing week. Verify the shard's origin without opening it, and check the public financing record separately.
completion: The shard is authentic and remains sealed. Its purchase was funded by Cinderwood restoration certificates. Sera asks for a copy of that entry.

title: The Unwritten Appendix
briefing: Post the Covenant charter's missing section at the Commons exchange: residents can receive care without keeping an archive or surrendering personal records.
completion: Residents add corrections beneath the notice. Sera schedules a review before filing the signed copy.

title: Cargo of Unasked Lives
briefing: Inspect the shipping route at the South floodgate. A manifest lists memory caskets left outside Vesper during the evacuation.
completion: Their destination was temporary storage. Sera starts tracing the delivery orders before arranging retrieval.

title: The Weatherproof Promise
briefing: Copy the recovered caskets' consent seals into the Last salt beacon's protected register. The original labels will not survive the heat.
completion: The seals have a durable copy and a custody record. The caskets stay closed during transport.

title: A Grave with a Network Address
briefing: Survey the caskets near the Last freshwater seep whose occupants declined revival. Find a retrieval path that avoids the proposed blanket sterilization.
completion: A narrow route is marked. Some caskets cannot be reached in time; their refusal records are copied before the crew withdraws.

title: The Hungry Catalog
briefing: Index drones are scanning the recovered caskets for voices. Disable them before the recordings reach the public catalog.
completion: The upload queue is stopped. Sera preserves the request list, with the voices sealed.

title: Permission to Disagree
briefing: At the Public memory archive, file two authorized accounts of Cinderwood's expansion beside the payroll and water records. One witness fed a family there; the other lost a spring.
completion: The payroll and stump totals support both witnesses. Sera retains both accounts without merging their conclusions.

title: The Cold Carrier
briefing: Wirejacks are cutting cooling jackets off the casket transport. Clear the collectors before the temperature rises past the safe limit.
completion: The cooling circuit holds. The keepers continue checking one consent seal at a time.

title: A Name Left Sealed
briefing: A recovered witness released a safety report but withheld their name. Publish it through the Memory vault without an identifying catalog entry.
completion: The engineers receive the warning. Sera checks the search index twice; the witness's name does not appear.

title: The Memory Dividend
briefing: Post the reduced storage plan at the Commons exchange. It funds clinic cooling by closing advertising and some immersive archives, instead of selling patient memories.
completion: Patients keep their records private. The virtual forest closes, leaving a transcript. Its donor cancels the next payment.

title: The Custodian’s Exception
briefing: Continuance has invoked an emergency exception to copy sealed records. Disable the wardens' extraction hardware while Sera challenges the unsigned order.
completion: The seals hold. The extraction log points to a replication service called the Inference Annex.

title: Lives between the Lines
briefing: Find the Inference Annex's mandate at the Public memory archive. It rebuilds withdrawn histories from public traces, then sells household profiles to water suppliers.
completion: Sera's deletion order covers the derived profiles as well as their source copies. The suppliers contest the order before the ink dries.

title: Not a Better Cage
briefing: Install independent consent checks at the Memory vault. Auditors need to see rule violations without opening the records themselves.
completion: The first audit flags an expired permission. Sera cannot override the seal with her own key.

title: Unlearning the Taken
briefing: Inference drones are carrying unauthorized profiles to roadside backups. Stop them before the copies disappear into the basin.
completion: The replica list stops growing. Sera sends the deletion order to every remaining address.

title: A Witness to Erasure
briefing: Register the last Annex deletion receipt at the Last salt beacon. Preserve the authority and time of deletion, without retaining the deleted records.
completion: The beacon accepts the receipt. A search of the replica returns an empty directory.

title: The Final Exception
briefing: Annex wardens are enforcing an order to preserve everything forever. Disable their extraction chassis while the keepers revoke that order.
completion: The Annex shuts down. Protected public records remain available through the ordinary vault controls.

title: A Door Opened from Within
briefing: Sera has made a decision about the missing week. Witness the Memory vault's permission check; leave the contents to Sera.
completion: The seal changes under Sera's key. In the next room, keepers sort records for the reduced cooling allowance.

title: Cold Storage
briefing: File the consent charter and the archive's actual water budget at Cinderwood's Stump ledger. Include the records being lost to low-power storage.
completion: The Annex is closed. Several immersive records survive only as text. Sera labels the empty shelf with the loss date and the cooling budget that forced it.

title: A Warm Place to Start
briefing: See that kitchen? Cold benches. Empty pot. A working pump behind a paid lock. We can fix two of those today. Pick up Oru’s welcome record first, then read the job notice at the Commons exchange. I will talk you through the water bypass. No heroics. Finish the job and come home.
completion: Pump steady. Benches warm. That is a day’s work, runner. Report back to Oru, then go see Nella by the kitchen. A bypass buys her a meal shift. Finding who keeps billing her buys us the next one.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Job sheet first. Walk to the Commons exchange in the middle of the plaza and press E. Find the shutoff order before you touch the pump.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: Two controls: the water meter and the kitchen tally. Press E at each. Disable the enforcement machines, then stay in the meter’s ring until the pump holds. Use a medkit if you need it.

steps.text: Record the bypass repair at the public forge. Press E, then return to Bram.
steps.voice: Hear that? A pump doing its job. Take the bypass settings to the Public forge and press E to log the repair. Then back to me. I want the next shift to know what we changed.

story.speaker: bram
story.invitation: You there, runner. Bram Cinder. Kitchen pump is sound; lock on the feed is not. Come to my marker. We have work to do.

title: The Bolt Nobody Owns
briefing: Three departments have stamped the cracked bracket. None has replaced it. Register a replacement pattern at the Public forge so Bram's crew can finish the job.
completion: The new bracket holds. Bram leaves the cracked one on the desk with all three stamps attached.

title: A Shift with an Ending
briefing: The pump crew's emergency rota has repeated for six months. Post relief shifts and protected breaks at the Commons exchange.
completion: The night crew clocks out. Their replacements get written handover notes and a working kettle.

title: Tools for the Living
briefing: Wirejacks are taking tools from an active water-line repair because the department was dissolved. Disable the collectors.
completion: The crew recovers its tools. Bram puts the current maintainers' names on the rack.

title: The Weight above Us
briefing: Inspect the Transit observatory span. Freight loads have been added to a bridge built for pedestrians, and the lower deck is reporting cracks.
completion: The stress marks match the freight timetable. Bram books an inspection with the residents beneath the span.

title: Heat without Tribute
briefing: The district heater cuts off homes with disputed bills. Change its control plate at the Public forge and post the fuel source beside the access rules.
completion: The cutoffs stop. Bram reads the woodpile estimate and schedules a separate meeting about the shortfall.

title: Safety Is a Stop Button
briefing: Audit drones restart machinery after workers hit the safety stop. Disable them before the crew opens the jammed feed assembly.
completion: The assembly stays still. The crew removes a bent gear with both hands clear of the drive.

title: The Last Apprentice
briefing: Retrieve the pump schematics from the Public memory archive. The only technician who knows the sequence has not had a day off in months.
completion: She corrects three errors in the drawing. Bram copies the corrections for the apprentices and approves her leave.

title: What the Pipe Carries
briefing: The pipe marked waste carries enough residual heat for two clinics. Register a pressure-limited exchanger at the Public forge.
completion: Both clinics receive heat. Downstream pressure stays within the marked limits.

title: The Cost on the Floor
briefing: Check Cinderwood's Stump ledger. Bram's fuel estimate leaves out lost shade, drying soil, and the cutters' treatment debts.
completion: With those costs included, the current bids fail. Bram cuts output. The cutters lose overtime first.

title: A Foundation Called Temporary
briefing: Read the Fen drawdown gauge before Bram approves another foundation patch. The supports are settling as the intake drains the bank.
completion: The dates match. Reinforcing the towers would leave the intake drawing at the same rate; Bram holds the purchase order.

title: Hands off the Relief Valve
briefing: A debt warden is blocking the emergency pressure valve. Shut it down so the engineers can open the relief line.
completion: The pressure drops into the safe band. The crew finishes the shift without a rupture.

title: The Shared Spare
briefing: Open the shared spare-parts register at the Public forge. Neighboring towers have compatible parts locked in separate stores.
completion: One tower's spare valve restarts another's pump. Both crews sign the replenishment sheet.

title: An Engine with No Heir
briefing: Find the original maintenance bond at the Public memory archive. Continuance is billing contractors' descendants for repairs they never agreed to perform.
completion: The bond names no consenting successor. Bram prepares releases for the workers and their families.

title: The Common Load
briefing: Publish the Common Load charter at the Commons exchange: rotating shifts, paid recovery, open budgets, and the right to stop unsafe work.
completion: Bram signs the same form as the crew. The removal procedure applies to his post too.

title: The Thirst under the City
briefing: Read the Concession sluice. Separate clinic cooling from the extraction scheduled to pay private dividends.
completion: The dividend schedule keeps pumping after the tanks fill. Canceling it helps, but clinic demand alone still exceeds summer recharge.

title: Reading the Dry Gauge
briefing: Recalibrate the Fen drawdown gauge to include recharge and the pump families' own water reserve.
completion: The revised report shows a deficit on ordinary days. Bram takes it to the assembly without changing the baseline.

title: The Scrap That Still Works
briefing: Wirejacks are stripping passive cooling fins needed for the intake conversion. Clear the collectors so the crews can recover the usable parts.
completion: The sound fins reach the site. Bram rejects a stack of cracked ones despite the shortage.

title: A Furnace Learns Patience
briefing: Set a slower furnace schedule at the Public forge. Reserve clinic power and cut commercial peaks first; list the paid shifts that will be lost.
completion: Upper-deck lights dim. The crew gets shorter shifts and a temporary wage guarantee. Next month's funding is still blank.

title: The People beyond the Drawing
briefing: Survey the Glassroot soil core before approving the new heat outlet. The proposed vent crosses root beds, and its hardware draws from Ada's mineral seam.
completion: The smaller outlet spares the roots but cools fewer rooms. Bram adds the waiting households to the revised plan.

title: An Alarm Nobody Must Hear
briefing: Connect the intake shutdown alarm to the Quiet array's light and vibration channels. Workers need to recognize it through masks, noise, or hearing loss.
completion: The crew identifies every signal in the test. The instructions go up beside each station.

title: The Debt Beneath the Debt
briefing: Trace the turbine surcharge at the Public memory archive. Prepare a retirement plan using a smaller replacement that leaves the Glassroot root mat intact.
completion: The turbine's repair costs exceed its useful reserve. The replacement covers essential loads; the remaining demand stays on the ration sheet.

title: A Machine Refuses Retirement
briefing: Audit drones keep restarting the turbine during conversion tests. Disable their restart network.
completion: The turbine remains idle. The replacement holds its rated load for the full test hour.

title: The Worker Is Not the Part
briefing: The turbine contract stores workers' memories as operating instructions. At the Memory vault, release authorized procedures and return control of private recollections.
completion: The engineers receive the procedures. Former crew members get separate notices asking what else, if anything, they wish to release.

title: The Weight We Can Share
briefing: Inspect freight limits and pedestrian access at the Transit observatory before foundation materials cross the span.
completion: Freight gets scheduled slots. The pedestrian lane stays open throughout the conversion.

title: The Emergency Ends Here
briefing: Turbine wardens are seizing workers for a compulsory final shift. Disable their restraints while delegates register the bond's termination.
completion: The workers are released. Enough sign up for the paid conversion shifts to cover the rota.

title: A Cool Night for Everyone
briefing: Start the overnight cooling test at the Public forge. Prioritize clinics and exposed homes, and publish the ration schedule and appeal address.
completion: The clinics hold temperature. Other rooms remain hot; Bram spends the rest of the shift reading appeals.

title: The Old Intake Falls Quiet
briefing: Wirejacks are swarming the retired intake. Clear the perimeter so trained crews can isolate hazardous sections before salvage begins.
completion: The safe metal goes into the common reserve. The contaminated chambers are sealed and marked.

title: No Final Heroic Shift
briefing: The last wardens insist on a worker inside the shutdown chamber. Disable them so the crew can use its remote release.
completion: The turbine stops with everyone outside. Bram counts the crew twice before signing off.

title: The Ground Holds
briefing: Read the Fen drawdown gauge after the conversion. Report recharge, ground settlement, and the cooling demand the new system cannot meet.
completion: Local drawdown has slowed. The deeper bore is still falling. Bram postpones a workshop roof to fund another reading.

title: After the Shutdown
briefing: Visit Cinderwood's Canopy refuge after the shutdown. Bram needs a fuel survey before deciding how the smaller furnace will handle the next heatwave.
completion: The canopy survives another season. Bram takes his first scheduled day off. An extraction lender's offer is waiting on his desk when he returns.

title: A Quiet Table
briefing: You can take a breath here. Nella’s kitchen has lost its water, and its warning never reached the people waiting for a meal. We will give them a working feed and a signal they can choose to hear. Speak with Oru, then read the notice at the Commons exchange. One step at a time. I am listening.
completion: Water in the kitchen. A warning light before the next interruption. A quiet place to sit. Small things, until you need them. Return your record to Oru. Nella is west of the exchange; let her tell you what is still missing.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: One step. The Commons exchange is in the middle of the plaza. Walk there and press E to read the notice. We will listen to what it leaves out.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: The silence was a shutoff, not consent. Follow the marker to both water controls. Clear the machines, then stay inside the meter’s ring. You do not have to do this alone.

steps.text: Connect the kitchen to the independent warning circuit. Press E, then return to Ves.
steps.voice: The feed is steady. Visit the Quiet array and press E to connect an independent warning. Come back when you are ready. We can let the room be quiet again.

story.speaker: ves
story.invitation: Welcome. I am Ves. Find me by the Commons. The kitchen needs water, and a warning people can hear. We can begin quietly.

title: Notice before Noise
briefing: The Quiet array starts its morning bulletin without warning. Add a visible countdown and a published schedule.
completion: The warning lamp comes on before the speakers. Residents have time to leave or switch channels.

title: The Attention Invoice
briefing: Fetch the attention contract from the Public memory archive. Continuance is fining residents who do not acknowledge broadcasts.
completion: The contract covers staffed emergency posts. Someone extended it to bedrooms; Ves marks the amendment and its signer.

title: A Pause without Penalty
briefing: Audit drones follow residents who leave a broadcast, repeating it louder. Shut down the pursuing units.
completion: The drones stop. A resident reads the same bulletin from the noticeboard and goes home.

title: A Route by Touch
briefing: Survey the handrails and landings at the Transit observatory. Spoken directions keep getting lost in the wind.
completion: The crew fits tactile and visible markers. A local walker tests the route before the old speakers come down.

title: The Invitation Frequency
briefing: Configure the Quiet array to offer a channel without opening nearby receivers. List the bulletin and let residents connect themselves.
completion: Receivers show the new channel. Those who select it hear the bulletin at the stated time.

title: The Broken Megaphones
briefing: Wirejacks are taking warning lamps while leaving the broken loudspeakers behind. Clear the collectors before the district loses its visible alarms.
completion: The lamps stay. The speakers go to the repair bench.

title: A Voice Kept Private
briefing: A former announcer's voice is still being used without permission. Check the release at the Memory vault and stop new announcements using that sample.
completion: The sample is withdrawn. Bulletins continue in the civic voice, with their transcripts intact.

title: Words of Our Own
briefing: The official phrasebook rejects complaints about the broadcast schedule. Open an attributed community board at the Commons exchange.
completion: The first notice complains about the Choir's meeting hour. Ves moves the meeting.

title: The Repeating Emergency
briefing: Find the old evacuation alarm's trigger at the Public memory archive. Retrieve the housing advertisement attached to it as well.
completion: The expired alarm is switched off. The homes advertised on reclaimed wetland still need a current flood warning.

title: Shelter from the Chorus
briefing: Survey a public path at Cinderwood's Canopy refuge. Amplified tours are disturbing the remaining nests, and the cutters rely on visitor income.
completion: The path opens without speakers, with a crowd limit. A tour company starts selling reservations for its own approach.

title: Silence Is Not a Command
briefing: Set local listening zones at the Quiet array. Keep space for the market's musicians and a usable route to the quiet table.
completion: The crew tests both areas during a performance. Ves leaves the master mute control disabled.

title: The Listener at the Wall
briefing: A warden has ordered the quiet-zone walls demolished as an obstruction to broadcasts. Disable its demolition controls.
completion: The walls remain. The crew checks that the public notices are still visible from both sides.

title: Hands in the Record
briefing: The Public memory archive files signed testimony as unidentified movement. Correct the catalog with the interpreters' attributed transcripts and visual records.
completion: The testimony is searchable. The interpreters retain access to correct translation errors.

title: The Listening Charter
briefing: Post the Listening Charter at the Commons exchange. Require accessible alternatives, named authors, emergency expiry dates, and an opt-out that preserves essential services.
completion: Ves signs it without an exemption for the Choir. The first review date is posted below.

title: Wind without Instructions
briefing: Survey the recorder range at the Glassroot soil core. Its wilderness channel hides kiln alarms and includes recordings from Ada's home.
completion: The household recordings are removed and the alarm channel is restored. The unedited feed contains wind, grinding ceramic, and a cough.

title: The Beacon Says Enough
briefing: Separate weather and rescue traffic from the Last salt beacon's compulsory announcements. Give warnings a location, an action, and an expiry.
completion: The test bulletin ends on time. The beacon returns control to the receiver.

title: The Voice That Chose Nothing
briefing: A Brine Bloom advertisement uses a resident's childhood voice without consent. Check the sample's release at the Memory vault.
completion: The resident gets the sample withdrawn. The company rerecords its recovery claim with a licensed speaker.

title: A Horizon of Speakers
briefing: Broadcast drones follow travelers beyond the beacon's coverage zone. Disable the mobile repeaters.
completion: The travelers leave the channel behind. The fixed beacon continues carrying weather alerts.

title: The Unheard Assembly
briefing: Meet the evacuation survey at the Last freshwater seep. Record the residents' requested warning terms and the route out of the outer settlement.
completion: The board shows the exit and supply schedule. The residents ask for fewer broadcasts, not fewer deliveries.

title: A Lamp in the Dust
briefing: Wirejacks are stripping the basin's storm-warning lamps. Clear the collection route before the dust front arrives.
completion: The lamp chain stays lit through the first grit. The same warning remains available in text and optional audio.

title: The Counter-Signal
briefing: The Quiet array treats every opt-out as a fault and raises its power. Add a signed refusal signal, and reserve the nesting refuge's quiet interval.
completion: The array accepts the refusal without boosting output. Ves tests it again after a receiver restart.

title: A Broadcast Can End
briefing: The Public memory archive records when emergencies begin but never when they end. Require an expiry and a named reviewer for priority broadcasts.
completion: The next permanent-emergency request is rejected. Its author must supply a review date.

title: The Volume Wardens
briefing: Wardens are raising amplifier power to override refusal signals. Shut down their controls while essential notices move to independent channels.
completion: The forced broadcast fades. The control ledger names its root order: universal attendance.

title: Attendance Is Not Assent
briefing: Retrieve the universal-attendance template from the Public memory archive. Find the clause that treats receipt of a message as acceptance of a contract.
completion: There is no signature field. Ves drafts a revocation covering every faction's broadcasts.

title: A Square with Several Sounds
briefing: Post the market celebration schedule at the Commons exchange. Include performances, quiet periods, an accessible route home, and the water and power allowance.
completion: The dance floor opens beside the quiet route. The music ends early to stay within the reserve.

title: The Last Uninvited Message
briefing: Repeater drones are flooding the channel with demands to acknowledge universal attendance. Disable them before they bury the approaching storm notice.
completion: The weather bulletin gets through. Ves keeps one copy of the compulsory demand for the case file.

title: A Network with an Exit
briefing: The Quiet array restores compulsory listening after a power loss. Save the districts' choices in local records and test recovery.
completion: The array restarts with the settings intact. Ves posts the recovery instructions beside the switch.

title: The Compulsory Chorus Falls
briefing: The root wardens still enforce universal attendance after its authority has expired. Disable them while the keepers revoke the order across the network.
completion: The root channel closes with an end notice. No acknowledgment is requested.

title: A Warning Worth Hearing
briefing: Test the Last salt beacon's final bulletin. Light, text, and optional voice must agree, then end on time. Keep the bloom evacuation boundary on the board.
completion: The test ends. A real distress call takes the freed channel while the crew checks the boundary markers.

title: The Next Marker
briefing: Return to the Last freshwater seep after the beacon test. Check the withdrawal boundary and record which warning stations are still reachable.
completion: Ves stands beside the abandoned houses. Wind moves through a broken window; fungal fans have reached the next marker. The crew moves the warning board back.

title: The Bowl before the Name
briefing: An empty bowl is our oldest greeting. Food first; names afterward. The kitchen has lost its water, so today that greeting needs your help. At the Commons exchange, read the shutoff notice. Help your contact restore the feed, then press E at the Lantern kitchen tally to reserve a bowl for the next arrival. Bring the record back to me.
completion: A place for you, and a place for someone we have not met. That is what this bowl means. Nella keeps the tally beside the kitchen. Ask her whose bowls stayed empty yesterday.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Take the welcome record to the Commons exchange. Press E to read the shutoff notice and help your contact restore the kitchen water. I will keep your place here.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: Food before an identity check. Keep that promise while you help your contact restore the water.

steps.text: Return to the kitchen and reserve a bowl for the next arrival. Press E, then return to Oru.
steps.voice: The kitchen can serve again. Press E at its tally to reserve the next arrival’s bowl. Then return to me.

story.speaker: archivist
story.invitation: Before you go to the exchange, come see me. I am Oru. Your welcome record belongs with your contact’s job. We can do both on the same trip.

title: The Children outside the Count
briefing: The shelter census lists fewer children than its surviving kitchen records fed. Compare the two accounts and recover the caregivers' handwritten additions before the archive treats those omitted lives as a clerical myth.
completion: Small names emerge from the margins of flour invoices. The Afterborn began with a practical refusal to let a missing record become a missing meal.

title: Strong Enough Together
briefing: A pamphlet credits Afterborn endurance to pure blood. Visit Mourning Fen's gauge and compare its clean-water record with the shelter's survival figures. Oru wants the filters and caregivers remembered, along with the marsh their work depended on.
completion: The figures follow water quality, not ancestry. The same wetland that kept the shelter alive is being drained to supply its descendants. Oru replaces the purity myth with a debt no ancestor knew how to repay.

title: The Unregistered Sick
briefing: Clinic audit drones reject patients whose ancestry records contain the old census gaps. Disable their screening loop so the clinic can treat immediate needs while its staff replaces the inherited eligibility rule.
completion: The waiting room begins moving by medical need. A damaged drone still prints ancestry fields that no nurse ever asked to use.

title: The Caregiver’s Last Page
briefing: A volunteer medic left one public recollection about the first shelter winter. Open the authorized testimony and recover the supply-sharing method they hoped later generations would improve instead of turning the medic into a flawless founder. The medic also records buying extra water through a concession that had displaced another shelter. Preserve that entry beside the supply-sharing method.
completion: The testimony includes mistakes, fatigue, and help accepted from strangers. Its final instruction is to revise the method when better knowledge arrives. The founder fed people by participating in a harm they could name and could not escape. The history keeps the contradiction.

title: Breath above Copper Walk
briefing: The lower clinics report the same cough each time hot air settles below the freight deck. Survey an upper crossing to compare airflow, showing that resilience cannot excuse leaving people in an environment that makes them ill.
completion: The pattern supports a ventilation repair and a shaded recovery route. Oru adds the evidence to the clinic budget instead of prescribing more endurance.

title: The Shelter That Walked
briefing: The old mobile kitchen stopped at Cinderwood's canopy before the forest became a fuel reserve. Visit the refuge and compare its shade with the shelter route. Oru needs to know which care stops still protect patients and which survive only as marks on a cherished map.
completion: Several old stops offer no shade at all. The food route kept people alive while its fuel purchases helped destroy the places they rested. The revised map removes no names, but crosses out shelters that are no longer there.

title: A Clinic on a Lamp Post
briefing: The roadside care route needs a reliable way to announce visits without publishing patients' names. Register a plain schedule at the salt beacon, including water supplies, accessible transport, and a channel for private requests.
completion: The first clinic notice reaches the basin shelters without exposing a single diagnosis. A practical old tradition gains a modern set of tools.

title: Medicine without a Toll
briefing: Salvage automatons are stripping the cooling packs from a public medicine carrier. Clear the route before the volunteers must choose between spoiled supplies and a dangerous rush across the salt.
completion: The medicine reaches the roadside stop within its safe temperature range. Oru records the delivery team as workers with support needs, not inexhaustible heroes.

title: The Survival Quota
briefing: A recovered shelter plan allocates care according to projected future labor rather than present need. Trace the outdated rule into the modern clinic system so the last hidden survival quota can be removed and publicly accounted for. The replacement must publish actual shortages instead of quietly translating a person's income into priority.
completion: The rule survived through copied software, long after the emergency that produced it. Its removal includes an audit for anyone whose treatment it delayed. Equal eligibility does not fill the medicine cabinet. Oru adds the missing supplies beside the rule so scarcity cannot hide behind a fair-looking form.

title: No Body Is a Forecast
briefing: Clinic wardens are enforcing the old labor forecast against patients outside its preferred age and ability ranges. Disable their admission controls while the staff installs an independently reviewable rule based on clinical need and equal dignity.
completion: The wardens lose the authority to grade a person's usefulness. The clinic opens its doors under a rule every patient can challenge.

title: The Care Ledger
briefing: Publish the roadside clinics' water allowance, staffing, and appeal contacts at the salt beacon. The care ledger must name the appointments the smaller reserve cannot yet support. Oru will not finance an unconditional promise by selling another wetland extraction claim.
completion: Care becomes a public duty with a visible waiting list. A family asks what a right means when treatment arrives too late. Oru leaves their question in the ledger without an answer underneath.

title: The Bowl beside the Empty Well
briefing: Walk the care route back to Mourning Fen. The survival quota is abolished, and everyone may bring a bowl. Measure the supply before the next meal; the Afterborn inheritance must include the source as well as the people gathered around it.
completion: Someone eats before being asked to prove their worth. Someone else waits while the pot is refilled with rationed water. The old exclusion is gone; the hunger that made it useful to its authors remains. Oru sets another bowl down. It is a necessary act, and it does not settle anything.

title: The Name You Answer To
briefing: Tell me the name you answer to. The welcome ledger still asks for a factory serial first. We will correct it, but Nella’s kitchen has lost its water and the people in that queue cannot wait. Read the Commons exchange notice, help your contact restore the feed, then press E at the Memory vault to record your chosen name. Return to me when it is yours.
completion: Your name comes first now. The serial stays in a repair record you control. You helped this city before it learned how to address you. Nella is west of the exchange; ask her about the people her ledger failed to count.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Take the welcome record to the Commons exchange. Press E to read the shutoff notice and help your contact restore the kitchen water. I will keep your place here.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: Your serial is not your introduction. First, help your contact bring the kitchen water back. We will put your name beside the response record.

steps.text: Record your chosen name beside the response log. Press E, then return to Oru.
steps.voice: A working feed. Now visit the Memory vault and press E to record the name you chose. Bring that introduction back to me.

story.speaker: archivist
story.invitation: Before you go to the exchange, come see me. I am Oru. Your welcome record belongs with your contact’s job. We can do both on the same trip.

title: Clay with a Memory
briefing: A ceramic repair pattern describes every cognitive mesh as interchangeable inventory. Inspect its thermal limits and mark the handling precautions that protect a living continuity during the ordinary work of replacing a cracked plate. The pattern lists Glassroot mineral as unlimited stock. Correct that claim using the kiln's remaining inventory.
completion: The repair guide begins with an introduction and a consent check. The same careful engineering now acknowledges who will experience the procedure. The inventory has an end date. A personhood notice can forbid treating a mesh as disposable without making its body permanent.

title: Two Witnesses, One Morning
briefing: Two witness shards preserve the same morning with different colors and distances. Compare their authorized metadata to learn how sensory calibration can change a recollection without turning either observer into a counterfeit person.
completion: Both records remain intact with their calibration notes. Oru invites you to describe your own senses without forcing them into somebody else's palette.

title: The Recall Order
briefing: Audit drones have mistaken a mesh safety notice for an order to repossess every Lattice using that ceramic batch. Disable their collection routine so technicians can offer voluntary repairs without detaining the people they intend to help.
completion: The safety warning stays public, but the seizure order ends. A repair invitation replaces the word recall on the neighborhood notice.

title: The Fork in the Census
briefing: The census merges two Lattice citizens because their memories share a history before a deliberate fork. Retrieve their separate declarations and establish the point where shared experience became two independent lives. Keep the two people's repair entitlements separate even though the kiln budget assumed only one shell would need maintenance.
completion: Both citizens keep their homes and appointments. Neither receives authority to cancel the other merely by claiming to be the original. The city owes two repairs from a reserve budgeted for one. Oru refuses to make recognition conditional on solving the shortage first.

title: A Signal Cannot Be a Self
briefing: A bridge repeater reports duplicate identities whenever both forked citizens cross its range. Survey the relay boundary and isolate the obsolete rule that equates a familiar handshake signal with ownership of a whole person.
completion: The repeater accepts distinct current keys without rewriting either past. Oru calls the result an engineering correction with room for philosophy later.

title: The Kilns beyond the Wall
briefing: The first witness vessels were fired from the Glassroot Steppe's mineral seam. Visit the northern soil core and compare its remaining depth with the root mat above it. Ada's kiln keeps people alive; expanding it would take the ground that keeps its well alive.
completion: The repair ledger and ecological survey describe the same material from opposite ends. Oru asks you to preserve both. There is no unowned spare world behind the one the plates came from.

title: Tam’s Ninth Cup
briefing: Ada's land register preserves Tam of Nine Cups' public request for a room with a door that locks from within. Retrieve it beside the mineral concession. The first recognized Lattice citizen asked for privacy in a body whose clay had already displaced a settlement.
completion: Tam's ordinary request remains just. So does the displaced families' claim to their well. Oru places neither underneath the other; the page now carries two needs the original ceremony kept apart.

title: The Pattern Harvesters
briefing: Salvage automatons are harvesting occupied mesh plates as reusable ceramic stock. Clear their collection route so the affected Lattice can recover damaged bodies under their own repair plans.
completion: The plates return to the people who recognize them. Unidentified fragments receive protected storage rather than an automatic merge.

title: A Seam Worth Keeping
briefing: An optimization service offers to smooth contradictory recollections by erasing whichever witness is less statistically common. Register a continuity instruction that preserves uncertainty and requires your permission before any future reconciliation.
completion: The service accepts a visible seam in the record. Oru observes that a life need not become perfectly consistent to remain yours.

title: The Merger Mandate
briefing: Continuance's wardens have classified independently living forks as an inefficient allocation of civic identity. Disable their forced-merger hardware while the archivists publish the separate declarations as binding records.
completion: The merger mandate loses its enforcement machinery. Each affected person receives a clear route to repair, housing, and services in their own name.

title: A Charter for Divergence
briefing: The city now needs a rule that outlasts this particular dispute. Register a charter protecting voluntary forks, chosen repairs, private memory boundaries, and the right of descendants to grow different from a shared past. Append the limited repair reserve and the right to challenge its allocation. No clause may describe a forced merger as environmental efficiency.
completion: The charter treats continuity as evidence to discuss, not a chain of ownership. It includes an appeal process led by people with varied experiences of identity. The charter protects divergence while bodies still need scarce ceramic. Oru refuses both compulsory unity and a false promise of limitless shells.

title: The Clay beneath the Self
briefing: Register the divergence charter at the Glassroot land office. It protects separate selves and closes the assumption that a living landscape is merely their stockroom. New repairs will depend on recovered ceramic, and the queue will be longer than anyone wants to announce.
completion: Forced merger ends. Ada patches another shell while grass grows through the abandoned extraction stakes. Some future repairs remain unfunded. The charter can forbid calling a person surplus; it cannot tell the seam to replenish itself. The door opens from within, onto the same exhausted ground.

title: A Second Introduction
briefing: You do not owe me the name you used before. I would like to know the person here now. Nella’s water has been locked, so let us begin with something the living need. Read the notice at the Commons exchange, help your contact restore the kitchen feed, then press E at the Relay terminal to leave your new introduction. Come back and tell me how you want it read.
completion: The channel carries your present name. The earlier one is yours to share or leave unspoken. Another beginning costs this city something; it does not give the city ownership of you. Nella keeps the kitchen just west of us. She could use your help.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Take the welcome record to the Commons exchange. Press E to read the shutoff notice and help your contact restore the kitchen water. I will keep your place here.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: You have returned before. Today, help the kitchen return. Follow your contact’s instructions at the water controls.

steps.text: Leave your new introduction on the neighborhood channel. Press E, then return to Oru.
steps.voice: Water is flowing. Leave your introduction at the Relay terminal with E, then come back to me. We will begin with the name you use now.

story.speaker: archivist
story.invitation: Before you go to the exchange, come see me. I am Oru. Your welcome record belongs with your contact’s job. We can do both on the same trip.

title: The Letter That Waited
briefing: A waiting letter was addressed to a former life and contains an invitation, not an obligation. Check its delivery seal without opening it so the vault can return control over the message to its intended living recipient.
completion: The letter receives a choice of when to open it, answer it, or leave it sealed. No reunion is scheduled on another person's behalf.

title: The Bond under the Covenant
briefing: Your lineage's early revival forms include a service bond hidden beneath the consent page. Retrieve the original terms and distinguish a volunteer's wish to live again from a contractor's attempt to purchase their future labor. The contractor counted a restored worker as renewable labor while treating the wetland supplying their body as free input.
completion: The forms reveal two agreements that should never have shared a signature. Oru begins a list of living people still charged against the old bond. Death was priced as a maintenance interruption. The depleted marsh never received an entry because it could not be billed for its own return.

title: Property of a Former Employer
briefing: Audit drones scan restored bodies for obsolete contractor marks and issue repossession orders. Disable their collection loop so affected Revenants can reach the clinic to remove those marks safely and voluntarily.
completion: The clinic queue moves without escorts. A body's manufacturing history stops being mistaken for a current claim of ownership.

title: Learning the New Hand
briefing: A restored worker keeps missing a tool grip because their new hand differs from the one they remember. Calibrate the forge's adaptive controls to the living body instead of requiring that body to imitate an archived movement perfectly.
completion: The worker finishes a careful first assembly with a new technique. Oru records adaptation as a skill, not evidence of failed restoration.

title: What Memory Cannot Promise
briefing: A restoration advertisement guarantees an unchanged return, even when the stored witness record is incomplete. Correct the public consent guide so future patients understand uncertainty, bodily change, and their right to seek support afterward.
completion: The guide makes no promise of a perfect copy. It promises honest information, continuing care, and recognition of whoever begins the next life.

title: Where the Barrier Ended
briefing: The barrier volunteers' memorial includes a water route from Mourning Fen. Visit its gauge and recover the support plan. The same contractors who promised rescue diverted supplies to profitable cooling loads while the barrier crew waited below the tide line.
completion: The rescue was possible on the original schedule. It became unprofitable after the diversion. The gauge bears no memorial for what happened downstream; its casing simply records a larger delivery to the city.

title: The Rescue That Was Delayed
briefing: A beacon log records why the barrier rescue arrived late: vehicles were held for an unpaid transport authorization. Recover the public incident record so the service bond cannot continue presenting a preventable delay as the workers' personal debt.
completion: The timeline places responsibility with the failed transport system. The volunteers' descendants receive a corrected public account with the original uncertainty preserved.

title: Caskets Are Not Cargo
briefing: Salvage automatons are cutting open dormant restoration caskets to recover their power cells. Clear the collection route so each intact casket can be handled according to the person's recorded wishes, including any refusal to return.
completion: The caskets reach protected custody without a mass activation. Oru checks consent before anyone begins counting potential rescues.

title: A Debt That Died Alone
briefing: Continuance transferred contractor debts across death while quietly dropping the contractor's duties of care. Publish the full bond history and challenge the one-sided inheritance on behalf of every restored person it still follows. The canceled service claim must not be replaced with a transferable lien on the materials used for a new body.
completion: The claim loses the missing context that made it look legitimate. The city recognizes no automatic labor obligation merely because a life has begun again. The debt ends without making restoration free to perform. The clinic's water allowance remains a separate, painful public argument.

title: The Repossession Wardens
briefing: The bond's wardens continue collecting Revenants under an order whose legal basis has collapsed. Disable their restraint chassis while the clinics distribute readable release records to everyone previously targeted.
completion: The collectors stop, and the releases do not require payment. Former contractors receive an appeal contact instead of another invisible queue.

title: The Right to One More Morning
briefing: The replacement revival covenant must protect both a wish to continue and a wish to decline. Register independent, revocable instructions with a review date so no faction, family, or creditor can substitute its preference for the person's own. State the present material limits honestly. A wish to continue must not authorize a creditor to drain the fen, nor a shortage authorize anyone to substitute refusal.
completion: The vault accepts either choice with the same care. Its consent screen no longer rewards one answer with brighter colors or easier buttons. The instruction protects a choice; it is no guarantee of the means to fulfill it. The vault records that uncertainty without charging for a brighter answer.

title: The Morning That Is Not Owed
briefing: Carry the corrected barrier history to the Brine Bloom's culture bank, where cultivated bodies begin. Register the new covenant beside the actual nutrient reserve. Neither the dead nor the landscape can be conscripted to make the city's survival account balance.
completion: The restoration bond is retired. Those who return owe no labor for the fact of being alive. Others remain in storage while cultures and water run short. Ilex watches a wild growth thrive beyond the bank without reviving anyone inside it. Life continues; the particular lives you hoped for are another matter.

title: The Garden You Carry
briefing: What do you call the life you carry? The welcome notice calls every symbiont a hazard. We can correct that, but first Nella’s kitchen needs water, for people and for its growing beds. Read the Commons exchange notice and help your contact restore the feed. Then press E at the Lantern kitchen tally to record individual care guidance. Return to me afterward.
completion: The notice now asks what care each person needs. The beds are watered, for tonight. We have changed a line on a screen; Nella has to make it work every morning. Find her west of the exchange and ask about the missing meals.

steps.text: Go to the Commons exchange and press E to read the shutoff notice.
steps.voice: Take the welcome record to the Commons exchange. Press E to read the shutoff notice and help your contact restore the kitchen water. I will keep your place here.

steps.text: Restore the kitchen water feed: repair both controls, clear enforcement, and hold the meter.
steps.voice: People and growing beds share this feed. Follow your contact to the controls; restore the water before we revise the care notice.

steps.text: Check the restored water feed with the kitchen growers. Press E, then return to Oru.
steps.voice: The feed is back. Press E at the Lantern kitchen tally to record the care guidance, then return to me. Tell me which words fit your partnership.

story.speaker: archivist
story.invitation: Before you go to the exchange, come see me. I am Oru. Your welcome record belongs with your contact’s job. We can do both on the same trip.

title: A Meal for Two Kinds of Life
briefing: The public nutrient mixer offers only the licensed formula sold to the original salt miners. Inspect an open formulation that supports several safe cultures and keeps its ingredients readable to the people who depend on them. Check its water and mineral requirements as carefully as its license. An open recipe can still exhaust a shared source.
completion: The mixer gains a carefully tested alternative with clear limits. Symbiont care no longer begins with a payment to an absent patent office. The formula is free to copy. The things it must eat are not made plentiful by that freedom.

title: The Unleased Bloom
briefing: An old company archive calls the first independent cultures stolen equipment. Recover the miners' own cultivation notes to show how they developed viable partnerships after the licensed nutrient supply became a tool of control.
completion: The notes describe years of shared experiments and failures. Oru restores the miners' names to a history that had credited only the company laboratory.

title: The Harvesters’ Mistake
briefing: Salvage automatons classify living symbiont cultures as recoverable industrial stock. Disable their collection route so the clinic can move its patients and samples without becoming a source of machine-selected raw materials.
completion: The clinic keeps its cultures under patient-approved care plans. The machines' inventory category is retained as evidence of the rule being challenged.

title: A Language of Changes
briefing: Early Sporebound diaries describe shifts in appetite, scent, and sleep that later catalogs turned into claims of a commanding hive mind. Review the voluntarily released notes and restore their careful observations of distinct partnerships learning to coexist. Retain the entries where a host's needs and a culture's growth did not agree. Coexistence was work, not a recovered natural harmony.
completion: The corrected archive separates chemical signaling from orders and individual experience from a whole lineage. Oru leaves space for the parts biology has not yet explained. One diarist chose a weaker culture to keep breathing through winter. Oru refuses to edit the compromise into a story of perfect partnership.

title: Where the Air Goes
briefing: A clinic plans to vent a culture room onto an upper walkway. Survey the airflow and public access so its new system can contain experimental spores without isolating ordinary Sporebound residents from the city around them.
completion: A filtered vent route protects the walkway. The clinic's safety plan applies to the experiment rather than to everyone who shares a lineage with its patients.

title: Green under the White
briefing: At the Brine Bloom's seep, industrial strains are escaping into the salt pans. Visit the boundary and compare living color with the suppliers' restoration claims. Oru wants a survey of who can survive this growth, not a photograph proving that something green exists.
completion: The fans are thriving where native communities and human households are failing. The supplier calls every new patch recovery. Oru records the losses alongside the spread; nature has not chosen a side anyone can inhabit without cost.

title: The Culture That Ate Its Neighbors
briefing: Read the Brine Bloom culture bank's mineral records. The licensed strain was bred to depend on a scarce feed; its feral descendants learned to draw from the seep instead. The response needs to distinguish an ended monopoly from an ecosystem made safe.
completion: The patent's hold is weaker and the pressure on the seep is greater. Oru marks the remaining refuges without promising that one emancipated organism will leave room for another.

title: No Blanket Cure
briefing: Continuance's treatment drones are spraying a broad sterilant that harms the refuges along with the industrial strain. Disable the spray units before their simple solution destroys the diversity the response is supposed to protect.
completion: The spray front stops at the marked boundary. The clinic replaces its borrowed pesticide plan with targeted removal and carefully contained trials.

title: The Patient Bioreactor
briefing: Configure a sealed bioreactor at the forge to test mixed cultures against the industrial strain. Include their water draw and waste heat in the comparison. A counter-culture that wins by consuming the last reserve would merely give the collapse another name.
completion: One mixed community slows the strain, but only while receiving nutrients the wider basin cannot supply. The result is useful inside a bounded refuge. Oru refuses the proposed headline announcing a cure.

title: The Quarantine Line
briefing: Wardens enforce an old industrial quarantine against Sporebound travelers while ignoring unsealed company sample crates. Disable the discriminatory checkpoint so inspectors can apply containment rules to actual materials and exposures.
completion: Travelers regain the route, and the sample crates finally receive inspection. The new boundary follows a documented hazard instead of a person's ancestry.

title: A Library That Stays in Its Jars
briefing: Register a diverse, sealed culture library at the Brine Bloom bank, with a limited water allowance and withdrawal boundary. The keepers can preserve samples and protect narrow refuges; they cannot restore the whole salt pan by releasing another organism with orders to win.
completion: The library opens. Families outside its defensible boundary receive relocation notices and a share of the remaining supplies. Nobody confuses the safety of the jars with the recovery of the place they came from.

title: The Pact Nobody Else Signed
briefing: Walk the Brine Bloom's remaining seep after the contained trials. Confirm the refuge boundary and record the growth beyond it, including the strains that now live without a supplier. Oru asks for a conclusion that does not turn survival into innocence or diversity into a promise of peace.
completion: The monopoly is broken. A few cultures remain in common care, and the wild bloom continues across the evacuated pans. Hosts and fungi keep negotiating needs that cannot all be met. The pact is an agreement among the people still here. Nothing in the salt has signed it, and nothing promises to wait for their next decision.

title: The Water beneath the Wage
briefing: Mara's overtime pays for water from the company draining her father's well. Read the Fen drawdown gauge so she can compare extraction with her shift records.
completion: The steepest drops match the best-paid shifts. Mara lays the overtime slips beside the readings.

title: A Share in the Thirst
briefing: The concession is offering shares instead of back pay. Retrieve the contract at the Concession sluice before Mara's crew signs.
completion: The shares carry no vote. Their dividend rises when pumping exceeds the wetland limit. Mara takes the contract back to the crew.

title: Enough for This Winter
briefing: Record Mara's settlement at the Concession sluice: lower extraction and a winter wage floor, paid for by canceling the dividend. The lease can resume after the guarantee expires.
completion: The pump slows. Mara can buy water through winter. The gauge remains well below its old high-water stain.

title: The Forest in the Prospectus
briefing: Check the Stump ledger west of Vesper. Tovin's restoration crew is being paid to cut living trees, with replacement seedlings already sold as mature timber.
completion: Most seedlings died in their first dry season. The nursery photograph on every certificate is eleven years old.

title: What the Canopy Keeps
briefing: Survey the soil at the Canopy refuge. Cutting the last shade trees would clear Tovin's treatment debt and expose the surviving seedlings to the heat.
completion: The shaded soil still holds water. Outside the canopy, roots crumble. Tovin's daughter's next treatment bill arrives that afternoon.

title: Standing Timber
briefing: Enter the cutters' actual yield and treatment debts at the Stump ledger. They will share the surviving wood and sell fallen timber, canceling the false restoration credits.
completion: The certificates collapse, taking the crew's pension reserve with them. Tovin sells his tools to keep his daughter's appointment. The living trees remain standing.

title: A Body in the Seam
briefing: Read the Glassroot soil core before Ada authorizes a deeper cut. Her partner needs replacement ceramic; the same seam supports the roots around the settlement's well.
completion: The deeper seam could supply years of repairs. Removing it would collapse the well within months. Ada asks to see the measurements again.

title: Vacant Means Unprofitable
briefing: Retrieve the mine survey from the Vacant land register. It lists the settlement as vacant, although Ada's neighbors are still living there.
completion: The surveyor recorded every house, then removed them from the valuation. The company offers the residents relocation loans.

title: The Road South
briefing: Register the settlement's departure at the Vacant land register and close the deeper extraction claim. The relocation grant carries no debt; salvaged ceramic will cover urgent repairs only.
completion: Ada loads her partner's patched shell onto a handcart. The families leave with a right to return and no date when they can use it.

title: The Green That Came Back Wrong
briefing: Inspect the Last freshwater seep before the spreading fungus reaches the refuge cultures. Ilex needs a water reading, not another photograph for the recovery prospectus.
completion: Licensed cultures and escaped strains are drawing from the same seep. The outer houses are already empty.

title: A Patent with No Heirs
briefing: Read the oldest lease at the Sealed culture bank. Continuance still charges hosts for propagating their partners even though the original owner is gone.
completion: The licensed strain depends on the supplier's scarce feed. Escaped descendants draw straight from the seep. Ilex records both in the lease challenge.

title: Outer Boundary
briefing: Register Ilex's containment plan at the Sealed culture bank. Cancel the propagation lease, seal the culture library, and withdraw the outer settlement with its remaining supplies.
completion: The bank closes its sales desk. Growth covers the evacuated houses. Ilex leaves one lamp burning for the next inspection.

title: The Empty Bowls
briefing: Fourteen bowls stayed empty yesterday. Your repair brought the water back, but it did not bring those people home. Start at the Lantern kitchen tally. Compare it with the Commons water meter, then return to the tally and save the names. I need the people, runner, not a better-looking total.
completion: Fourteen names. Thank you. We keep their bowls here. Now we need to find out why a donated jug costs its donor another payment. I have the next job ready for you.

title: A Gift Charged Twice
briefing: There: the same jug, billed twice. Read the Commons water meter with E. When the concession locks the feed again, help restore both controls, clear its machines, and hold the meter’s ring. Read the meter once more afterward. We need the before and after on the same page.
completion: Same serial, two charges. There is our proof. The kitchen is running again, but I cannot stand at that meter all night. One more job: help us share the work.

steps.voice: The lock is back. Restore the two controls, clear the machines, and hold the meter’s ring. We can try again if this shift runs out.

story.speaker: nella
story.invitation: I found the same jug on two bills. Come back to the kitchen. Let us put the before and after on the same page.

title: Who Washes the Bowls
briefing: Soup does not wash its own bowls. Post our rota at the Open pantry ledger with E. Spend ten seconds beside the Commons water meter to check the feed, then return to the ledger and confirm the handover. Everyone gets a turn, including me getting a turn to sit down.
completion: There. Someone else has the ladle. The portions are still small, but no one gets billed twice for sharing. You know this block now, runner. Your faction contact has more work when you are ready.

steps.text: Publish the neighborhood rota.
steps.voice: Go to Open pantry ledger. Press E to inspect the record.

steps.voice: Stay by the water meter for ten seconds. A steady feed is worth checking before you hand it to the next shift.

steps.text: Confirm the handover on the duty board.
steps.voice: Go to Open pantry ledger. Press E to inspect the record.

story.speaker: nella
story.invitation: One more thing, runner. A shared meal needs a shared shift. Come back and help me put the rota into practice.

title: An Ordinary Morning
briefing: Visit the Unsorted witness shelf. Elin needs to know whether the discarded record was unwanted, or merely unprofitable. Compare both marked records, then return to the first to preserve what disagrees.
completion: The witness wanted that morning kept. A clerk places the request beside its disposable label and waits for an explanation.

title: The Warmest Shelf
briefing: Read the Cooling priority console and find what decides which memories remain cold. The block is facing another emergency: memories running warm. Read the service record, help resolve the live incident, then record the outcome.
completion: Elin isolates the payment sort. Technicians begin marking redundant cabinets instead of asking families to outbid each other.

title: Room for One Copy

completion: Families share the available cold space. Some copies are lost by permission. Elin keeps the refusals in the same ledger as the savings.

completion: The crew adds twenty-three households to its work sheet. The official vacancy count stays pinned underneath, where everyone can see the difference.

completion: Neighbors check the pulses against the lamps. The failure light is added to the inspection sheet, not hidden beneath a successful demonstration.

completion: Ivo posts the exclusion rule beside the board. The mechanic starts checking the late lift while the workers negotiate its hours.

completion: The late lift keeps its crew. There are fewer connections than the workers wanted, but the final one has a published time and someone responsible for keeping it.
